openings.claim: Hypothesis: replace inherited allocations with a needs-based schedule; improvement depends on compatible demand fitting available room-times, including piano requirements.
openings.discriminator: More needs met than incumbent under identical demand supports allocation mismatch; infeasible concentrated demand despite slack limits this mechanism.
openings.probe: Interview contacts by telephone/in person for weekly needs, acceptable windows, equipment and minimum usable duration. Compare incumbent and paper candidate across eight weeks, locking performances and weekly guarantees; seek agreement before changes. Do not count 60 minutes as satisfying longer needs.
openings.uncertainty: Contact reliability and feasibility remain unproven; blank equipment entries establish no flexibility. Stop adoption if constraints fail.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: an authoritative ledger, numbered bookings/changes, explicit supersession and room/date/time readback reduce conflicts and reconciliation if inconsistent records or unacknowledged changes contribute.
openings.discriminator: Fewer copy disagreements and conflicts support record causation; conflicts despite matching current confirmations suggest communication, interpretation or another cause.
openings.probe: Update the desk ledger before verbal confirmation; mark online-copy updates and times. Track identifiers, conflict circumstances and total administration including recording/readback overhead throughout eight weeks.
openings.uncertainty: Volunteer/desk consistency is assumed; added work may exceed reconciliation savings. Neither record errors nor scheduling is established as dominant; missed-session causes/recoverability remain unknown.

lineage.reason: Compatibility feasibility and reassignment gates preserved.
Needs-based operation and comparable-demand test preserved.
Supersession, confirmation order and overhead dependency preserved.

decision: Test both hypotheses. Preserve two rooms, existing equipment, 24 staffed hours/week, no new fees, both performances, telephone/in-person booking/changes without mandatory digital accounts, and a requested weekly 60-minute slot when any opening is acceptable. Success requires >=90% stated needs within acceptable windows, fewer than two conflicts and <=120 administration minutes/week averaged over eight weeks; the needs denominator is currently unknown.
